jobs.title: Lead Analyst, Business Operations & Strategy
jobs.description:
About Figure 
 Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. The fastest growing components are Figure Connect, its credit marketplace, and Democratized Prime, Figure’s on-chain lend-borrow marketplace. Figure’s ecosystem also includes DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) for asset custody and lien perfection, and $YLDS, a yield-bearing stablecoin registered with the SEC as a security under the Securities Act of 1933.
Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.
We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies .
 About the Role 
 As a Lead, Business Operations, you will sit at the center of Figure’s most important decisions, translating strategy into execution across Figure’s Lending and Digital Assets businesses, and ensuring leaders have clear, timely, and actionable insight into how the business is performing.
 This role is a hybrid of business planning, executive reporting, and strategic problem-solving. You will work on core components of quarterly planning, forecasting, and budgeting; drive weekly and monthly executive reporting against company goals; and lead analyses that directly inform decisions made by Figure’s executive team. You’ll partner closely with leaders across Finance, GTM, Product, Analytics, Operations, and Capital Markets to align priorities, surface tradeoffs, and scale Figure’s operating rhythm as the business grows.
 This is a high-visibility role for someone who enjoys operating in ambiguity, improving processes, and taking ownership of work that matters. You’ll have exposure to both a scaled lending platform and a rapidly evolving digital assets business, making this a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of fintech and blockchain.
 What You’ll Do 
 Support business planning and execution across the entire company, including quarterly planning, goal-setting, and ongoing performance tracking against goals
 Lead executive reporting (weekly, monthly, quarterly), ensuring leadership has a clear, consistent view of volume, pipeline health, economics, and key operating metrics
 Drive critical components of budgeting and forecasting, partnering with Finance to translate strategy into forward-looking plans and identify risks and opportunities early
 Create high-impact analyses on complex, ambiguous questions, framing problems, synthesizing data, and delivering clear recommendations to senior leadership
 Serve as a connective layer across Finance, GTM, Product, Capital Markets, and Data, aligning stakeholders and ensuring decisions are grounded in shared facts
 Refine frameworks and operating tools (dashboards, scorecards, planning templates) that improve visibility, accountability, and decision velocity
 Scale the operating model as the business grows, identifying gaps, simplifying processes, and helping leadership stay focused on what matters most
 What We Look For 
 BA / BS degree or equivalent practical experience
 3+ years of experience in investment banking, management consulting, strategy, or business operations at a high-growth company; investment banking highly preferred 
 Strong analytical skills with the ability to move quickly from data to insight to recommendation, including ability to build and refine models
 Proven ability to work cross-functionally and influence without authority, including with senior stakeholders
 Excellent organizational and project management skills; comfortable owning multiple high-stakes workstreams in parallel
 High judgment, intellectual curiosity, and comfort operating in a fast-moving, constantly evolving environment
 Experience supporting or partnering with sales, GTM, or revenue teams
 Interest in digital assets, capital markets, and/or DeFi is a plus
 Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures
 Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes
 Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team

 25% annual bonus target, paid quarterly 
 Company equity in the form of RSUs

While most offers are generally made within the middle of the range, final compensation is determined based on the factors above.

jobs.title: Senior AI Machine learning Engineer
jobs.description:
Summary 
Guidewire’s Generative AI (GenAI) team sits within Product Strategy and plays a critical role in shaping the future of our cloud and AI-powered platform for P&C insurers worldwide. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams to embed AI, cloud, and data capabilities across the portfolio, enabling secure, scalable, and reliable solutions for our customers. You’ll join a highly collaborative, hands-on engineering culture focused on experimentation, learning, and shipping production-grade AI at scale. 
As a Senior ML Engineer, Generative AI, you will be a technical leader driving the design, development, and operation of Guidewire’s end-to-end GenAI solutions and Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities. You will own critical components of our LLM infrastructure, from data pipelines and prompt engineering through fine-tuning, deployment, and monitoring of models in production. This role is ideal for someone who wants to shape next-generation AI solutions that directly power insurance workflows, support our Agentic AI product vision, and help deliver measurable outcomes for customers globally. 
 Job Description 
 What you’ll do
 Lead the design, implementation, and evolution of Guidewire’s GenAI and LLM products, including data ingestion, feature pipelines, model training, fine-tuning, deployment, and monitoring on AWS (e.g., S3, EC2, RDS, SageMaker).
 Architect and build robust ML/LLM pipelines that power high-impact use cases such as claim summarization, underwriting assistance, pricing and rating intelligence, and developer productivity tools across our product portfolio. 
 Develop and optimize LLM solutions using techniques such as prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, and fine-tuning to deliver reliable, safe, and high-performing experiences for insurance users.
 Collaborate with Product Strategy, PDO, and Professional Services teams to align GenAI capabilities with the broader Product VPMOM, Agentic AI product roadmap, and customer adoption goals (including Claims Summary, Underwriting Assistant, Codelift, and other GenAI “lifts”). 
 Establish and apply ML Ops best practices for CI/CD, experimentation, evaluation, observability, and responsible AI, ensuring models are auditable, secure, and production-ready at scale. 
 Mentor and coach engineers and data scientists, conduct code and design reviews, and champion technical excellence, including performance, reliability, and cost efficiency of AI workloads.
 Partner with cross-functional teams (Security, Finance, BizTech, GTM) to ensure AI solutions adhere to data governance and security controls, and contribute to Guidewire’s mission to transform how P&C insurers do business through cloud, analytics, and AI. 
 At Guidewire, we foster a culture of curiosity, innovation, and responsible use of AI—empowering our teams to continuously leverage emerging technologies and data-driven insights to enhance productivity and outcomes. 
 What you’ll bring
 Required
 Demonstrated ability to embrace AI and apply it to your current role as well as data-driven insights to drive innovation, productivity, and continuous improvement. 
 5+ years of professional experience in Machine Learning and/or Data Science, including end-to-end delivery of production ML systems.
 Deep expertise in Python and experience building scalable ML/LLM services and pipelines, ideally on AWS using services such as S3, EC2, RDS, and SageMaker.
 Strong understanding of ML Ops practices for model development, deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management (including CI/CD for ML, experiment tracking, model registries, and drift detection).
 Hands-on experience with classical and gradient-boosting models (such as GLM, Random Forest, and XGBoost) and their application to real-world business problems.
 Deep understanding of neural networks and transformer-based architectures for LLMs and chat models, including familiarity with open-source foundation models and their fine-tuning and inference.
 Experience with prompt engineering, RAG and related LLM architecture patterns, and vector databases for semantic search and retrieval.
 Solid knowledge of evaluating and monitoring LLM performance using NLP and LLM-assisted metrics, with a focus on safety, robustness, and user experience.
 Demonstrated technical leadership: driving design decisions, leading complex engineering efforts, mentoring peers, and conducting thoughtful code and architecture reviews.
 *****MUST HAVE GUIDEWIRE EXPERIENCE******* 
 Preferred
 Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
 Experience building data pipelines and features using SQL, Spark, or AWS Glue.
 Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and creating backend APIs to expose ML/LLM services.
 Familiarity with CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code practices and tools such as TeamCity and Terraform.
 Background in insurance, banking, or financial services, or interest in becoming deeply fluent in P&C insurance to better shape high-value AI and GenAI use cases.

 We believe in clarity and setting you up for success. jobs.title: Senior IT Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Alloy is where you belong!
 Alloy is the AI-powered identity and fraud prevention platform that accelerates onboarding, stops fraud, and scales compliance across the customer lifecycle so financial organizations can grow without limits. More than 900 of the world's leading financial institutions and fintechs trust Alloy for smarter risk management that drives growth.
 Through our values: Be Bold, Go Fast, Collaborate, and Celebrate Our Differences, we are creating a workplace where you can grow, thrive, and belong.
 See how we've been continuously recognized and named one of Inc. Magazine's Best Workplaces , Forbes America's Best Startup Employers , Best Fintech to Work for by American Banker, year after year.
 Check out our investors and read more about us here .
 About the team
 The IT and Security team controls who and what can reach Alloy's systems, from the laptops our people use to the SaaS tools and AI agents they work in. Our customers are banks and fintechs, and our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 programs depend on access controls that hold up under audit. We run as a shared-responsibility team: each engineer is the go-to expert in their area and backs up teammates across the rest.
 Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. Given the internal client-facing nature of this role, the in-person office attendance requirement is four days per week (Tuesday-Thursday, with your choice on whether the fourth in-person day is Monday or Friday).
 What you'll do
 You'll own workforce identity at Alloy, from how access is granted and automated to how it is reviewed and removed. You'll be the primary expert for Okta, SaaS access, and identity automation while sharing coverage for broader IT and Security work.
 IAM and Okta Administration: Serve as the primary technical SME for workforce identity and access management, including Okta groups, policies, application assignments, admin roles, MFA, and authentication controls.
 SaaS Access and Integrations: Manage SaaS access and application onboarding. Implement and maintain SSO integrations using SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning, and Google Workspace access.
 Identity Lifecycle and Automation: Maintain and improve employee and contractor joiner/mover/leaver workflows from our HRIS through our IdP and downstream SaaS. Use Okta Workflows and other automation to cut manual access processes.
 Access Operations: Troubleshoot authentication and provisioning issues, administer temporary access and exceptions, and make access requests more reliable and efficient.
 RBAC Management: Refine, manage, and evolve Alloy's approach to role and attribute based access control.
 Privileged Access Management: Mature PAM/TPAM for administrator and production resource access, including just-in-time and temporary access and break-glass procedures.
 Non-Human Identity Management: Improve ownership and lifecycle controls for service accounts, system users, API credentials and tokens, OAuth applications, bots, and integrations.
 AI Identity and Access: Shape identity and delegated-access controls for AI platforms, AI agents, and MCP integrations, including the scope of access available to tools and agents.
 Access Governance and Compliance: Strengthen least privilege and RBAC/ABAC, run access and privileged-access reviews, remediate stale or orphaned accounts, enforce contractor access expiration, and provide IAM evidence for ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
 Shared IT/Security Engineering: Take on endpoint security, EDR, DLP, application control, email security, SaaS/security tools, and other IT/Security projects within a shared-SME and backup-coverage model.
 Incident Response and Collaboration: Investigate incidents involving identity, users, endpoints, email, and SaaS. Coordinate with teammates and business partners, and keep processes and documentation clear.
 On-call Rotation: Join the IT and Security on-call rotation, responding to critical alerts and urgent after-hours support requests.
 What we're looking for
 Must-haves:
 Hands-on experience in IT or security engineering, with significant responsibility for Okta or a comparable workforce identity provider
 Experience administering IdP groups, access and authentication policies, SaaS application assignments, MFA, and administrative roles
 Experience implementing and troubleshooting SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM provisioning, and OAuth-based integrations
 Experience running employee and contractor identity lifecycles across HR systems, an IdP, Google Workspace, and downstream SaaS applications
 Ability to automate access workflows using Okta Workflows, APIs, scripts, or comparable tools
 Understanding of least privilege, RBAC/ABAC, access reviews, and account lifecycle controls
 Working familiarity with endpoint security, EDR, DLP, email security, and SaaS security tooling, and willingness to work beyond IAM
 Strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills in a shared-responsibility IT/Security team
 Nice-to-haves:
 Experience with temporary privileged access management platforms
 Experience governing non-human identities, service accounts, API credentials, and OAuth applications
 Familiarity with identity and delegated access for AI tools, agents, and MCP integrations
 Experience with ISO 27001 or SOC 2 controls in a fintech, SaaS, or other regulated environment
 Alloy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Below is the anticipated starting base compensation range for this role; however, pay may vary depending on job-related knowledge, in-demand skills, relevant experience, and/or geography. In addition to a competitive base salary, this position is also eligible for equity awards in the form of stock options (ISOs) as well as a competitive total benefits package. Your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details and what compensation could look like for you specifically!
 This position has a base salary range of $162,000 – $190,000. 
 Benefits and Perks
 Unlimited PTO and flexible work policy
 Employee stock options
 Medical, dental, vision plans with HSA (monthly employer contribution) and FSA options
 401k with 100% match up to 4% of annual employee compensation
 Eligible new parents receive 16 weeks of paid parental leave
 Home office stipend for new employees
 Annual learning & development stipend
 Well-being benefits include access to ClassPass, OneMedical, UrbanSitter, and Spring Health
 Hybrid work environment: our employees local to NYC are expected to work Tuesdays through Thursdays from our HQ in Union Square, Manhattan. Tasty lunches catered from a variety of local restaurants and frequent employee-organized cultural events contribute to our positive office energy. On Monday/Friday, most employees Zoom into work from home while some take advantage of the quieter office.
 How to Apply
 Apply right here! You've found the application!
 Alloy is proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace and employer. We're committed to equal opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, gender, gender identity, parental or pregnancy status, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or veteran status. We are committed to an inclusive interview experience and provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with visible and invisible disabilities. We encourage applicants to share needed accommodations with their recruiter.
 All Alloy jobs are listed on our careers page. Any communication during the recruitment process, including interview requests or job offers, will come directly from a recruiting team member with an alloy.com email address. We do not use outside applications or automated text messaging in our recruiting process. We will not ask for any sensitive financial or identification information during the recruiting process. If you're ever unsure, please contact us directly via our website before sharing personal information.

You'll own Socure's most important channel relationships in financial services, including core banking providers, digital banking and account-opening platforms, banking-as-a-service providers, and systems integrators. You'll act as the connective tissue between partners and Socure's Sales, Product, Marketing, and Legal teams, turning partnerships into a repeatable source of revenue.

This is a senior, quota-carrying role for a partnerships leader who knows how financial institutions buy technology and who can build trust at the executive level. You'll own partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue and shape how Socure scales across the financial services market.





WHAT YOU'LL DO


PARTNER STRATEGY & DEVELOPMENT

 - Define and execute a channel strategy for financial services that identifies the partners, partnership models, and target segments that will drive the most revenue.

 - Recruit, negotiate, and close new strategic partnerships, including referral, reseller, embedded, and OEM agreements, in partnership with Legal and Finance.

 - Build joint business plans with each strategic partner, with clear revenue targets, target accounts, integration milestones, and go-to-market commitments.


CHANNEL SALES & PIPELINE

 - Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue targets for financial services.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL PARTNERSHIP

 - Partner with Marketing on joint campaigns, events, content, and co-branded materials that build demand with partners' customer bases.

 - Train partner sales and solutions teams on Socure's products, value propositions, and ideal customer profile so they can position Socure with confidence.

 - Bring partner feedback, market insights, and competitive intelligence into Socure's product and go-to-market planning.

 - Establish and track KPIs tied to partner-sourced pipeline, partner-influenced revenue, partner activation, and deal velocity.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 10+ years of enterprise sales or business development experience, with at least 5 years in channel sales, strategic alliances, or partnerships at a financial services technology company.

 - A track record of meeting or exceeding partner-sourced revenue targets and closing complex, multi-party deals.

 - An established network across banks, credit unions, and the technology providers that serve them, such as core banking, digital banking, and banking-as-a-service platforms.

jobs.description:
About AlphaSense:  
 AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com . Come join us. 
 About the Team: 
 Working hand-in-hand with our Directed Content and 1x1 Call Services groups, this team provides timely channel checks and voice-of-customer interviews that reveal real-time demand signals, competitive dynamics, and purchasing behavior across priority industry verticals. By identifying the right operator, distributor, or end-customer profiles—and engaging them at the optimal moment in the quarter—we help investors surface differentiated, actionable insights.
 Channel & Customer Research (CCR) delivers scalable primary research that provides real-time insight into company performance and industry conditions. Through structured interviews with distributors, resellers, suppliers, consultants, and other channel partners, CCR captures the perspectives of professionals directly involved in how products and services move through the market. Leveraging AlphaSense’s AI Interviewer technology, CCR is able to conduct and scale structured expert interviews continuously, expanding coverage while maintaining consistency and analytical rigor. Covering hundreds of companies across major sectors, CCR provides investors and corporate users with channel research that offers a continuous view of demand trends, competitive dynamics, and market conditions as they develop.
 About the Role: 
 Analysts are the execution engine for our Channel and Customer Research offering. 
 You will:
 Map the expert universe for assigned verticals
 Source and vet high-value channel partners and customers
 Build long-term relationships with key channel sources
 Coordinate and monitor interviews
 Form sector expertise through regular and consistent research to remain up-to-date on industry trends and news
 This role blends investigative research, stakeholder management, and rapid-fire project execution—perfect for early-career professionals eager to accelerate their learning curve inside a high-growth, data-driven organization.
 Who You Are: 
 Energetic Team Player: You have a proven ability to manage fast turnaround projects, meet deadlines and targets while maintaining a team-first mentality.
 Adaptable: You are a creative problem solver who is comfortable with changes and new challenges. You thrive in ambiguity and remain resilient when faced with adversity.
 Inquisitive: You are naturally interested in learning and quickly see patterns that help you to identify the best possible experts for a given research project.
 Organized: You have demonstrated an ability to handle and prioritize multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously and autonomously
 Detail Oriented: You have a strong attention to detail, with the ability to discern and precisely document the core elements of an expert’s relevant skills or experience vis-a-vis a defined scope. 
 Excellent Communicator: You’ll regularly be engaging with industry experts to learn about their background and convey what it means to participate in our network. You are comfortable with all communication methods, including phone and email.
 Goal Oriented: You are motivated by the idea of identifying and delivering the best-possible expert profiles for each project scope quickly and efficiently
 What You’ll Do: 
 Expert Sourcing & Outreach: Drive email, phone, and LinkedIn campaigns to recruit best-fit experts; negotiate honoraria that balance insight value with cost discipline.
 Screening & Onboarding: Conduct vetting calls to confirm role, recency, and perspective; ensure compliance with AlphaSense and client guidelines.
 Landscape Research: Develop and maintain target lists of distributors, resellers, customers, and other market participants aligned to quarterly coverage priorities.
 Interview Guide Creation: Build and maintain interview guides targeted to each type of call, industry sector, and expert profile - ensuring the best and most relevant insights are captured.
 Interview Facilitation: Schedule sessions at optimal times in the sell-side calendar; monitor calls, troubleshoot tech issues, and capture real-time highlights.
 Quality & Compliance: Uphold rigorous data-privacy standards and maintain accurate records in internal CRM and workflow tools.
 Continuous Improvement: Share feedback on talk tracks, sourcing tactics, and emerging themes to refine our playbooks and coverage roadmap.

jobs.description:
Who are we?

Our mission is to scale intelligence to serve humanity. We’re training and deploying frontier models for developers and enterprises who are building AI systems to power magical experiences like content generation, semantic search, RAG, and agents. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. We like to work hard and move fast to do what’s best for our customers.

Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are passionate about their craft. Each person is one of the best in the world at what they do. We believe that a diverse range of perspectives is a requirement for building great products.

Join us on our mission and shape the future!



Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans - by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting text output, you will improve Large Language Model’s performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere’s tech.


Cohere seeks dynamic and dedicated Data Annotators with exceptional Modern Standard German Writing, Translation, and Data Manipulation skill.



Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada. We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 30 CAD/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 - Bring Your Own Device (laptop). Remote work within Canada. 12 months contract. Performance incentives included!



As a Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Label and Rank: Accurately label and rank machine learning data with advanced proficiency in German, ensuring data integrity and quality.

 - Audit and Correct: Scrutinize and rectify any inaccuracies in language data (may include text, image, JSON, TSV/CSV, Markdown), maintaining the highest standard of data accuracy.

 - Reading and Text-Based Tasks: Efficiently complete reading and text-based assignments, with high attention to detail.

 - Preference-Based Tasks: Evaluate and complete tasks, assessing which responses in German best conform to project guidelines.

 - Recommend Optimizations: Identify and suggest opportunities for improving data quality and model performance in German language tasks.

 - Provide Feedback: Collaborate and communicate effectively, providing feedback to cross-functional team members, particularly on German language-related matters.

 - Detail-Oriented Execution: Maintain meticulous attention to detail while performing repetitive and precise tasks, particularly when working with language data.



You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Language Proficiency: Native or near-native proficiency in German; excellent command over English.

 - Expert reading and writing skills - which you are ready to prove on our written test.

 - Basic familiarity with JSON/TSV/CSV/Markdown data manipulation.

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy - you’re the type to proofread all of your emails!

 - High tolerance for repetitive and monotonous work.

 - Ability to follow complex instructions, navigate ambiguity and work independently.

 - Superb sense of urgency and time management.

 - Curiosity about technology and a knack for tackling problems in creative ways.

 - A reliable laptop.



The Candidate Journey:
Initial Screening - Once you have submitted your application our Talent Team will review your resume and writing samples.
Virtual Annotation Test -  This assignment will test your written skill through various language-based tasks, such as a a writing sample, interacting with a chat bot, and more.
Video Screen - If selected to move forward, you will have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team!

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
jobs.location: San Francisco; Remote (United States); Toronto; Seattle; New York City
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
jobs.location: San Francisco; Remote (United States); Seattle; New York City
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

 - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

 - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

 - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

 - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

 - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

 - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

 - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

 - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

 - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch.

 - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar).

 - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

jobs.title: Office Manager
jobs.description:
About Glean: 
 Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. 
 At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. 
 Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. 
 If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. 
About the Role:
 We’re looking for a highly organized and proactive Office Manager to lead day-to-day operations at our office. You’ll be essential in creating a smooth, welcoming, and productive environment—ensuring everything from facilities to vendor coordination runs efficiently.
 You will:  
 Develop and implement office policies and procedures to ensure smooth operations. 
 Order and manage office supply inventory 
 Manage F&B for our South Bay office 
 Maintain Badging procurement for employees and new hires 
 Plan and execute monthly employee engagement events 
 Facilitate effective communication channels within the office, ensuring timely and accurate dissemination of information. 
 Oversee maintenance and repair activities, ensuring the office is clean, safe, and well-maintained. 
 Liaise with vendors, contractors, and suppliers for office-related services, equipment and F&B. 
 Manage office equipment and technology, including computers and printers. 
 Address any facility issues promptly and efficiently. 
 Assist with collecting, cleaning, and resetting laptops 
 Monitor and manage office budgets and expenses 
 Serve as a point of contact between employees, management, and external stakeholders               
 Coordinate with the finance department for expense tracking and reporting.  
 About you:  
 Strong organizational and multitasking skills with the ability to prioritize tasks. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
 Proficiency in office software tools (e.g., MS Office, spreadsheets, database management). 
 Ability to handle confidential information with discretion. 
 Strong attention to detail and accuracy. 
 Problem-solving and decision-making abilities. 
 Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment. 
 Location:   
 This role is onsite (5 days a week in our Mountain View office)
 Compensation & Benefits:
 This role will be a 6 -month contract position with the possibility of extension and/or conversion based on performance and company needs. The range for this position is $35-$45/ hour. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.
 We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race.
#LI-ONSITE
 AI-First Mindset at Glean: 
 At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required.

Harvey's Finance Engineering team is the investment-side counterpart to our Legal Engineering team: former investment professionals who bring real deal experience to Harvey's prospects and customers. Forward Deployed Finance Engineers lead discovery, demos, pilots, trainings, onboarding, and custom builds alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real investment work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

Finance Engineers work on Harvey Deals, a new product built off of Harvey's acquisition of Benchmark. Harvey Deals is where investment teams run their deals — screening, underwriting, diligence, and committee materials — built in the firm's own templates and formats, with every figure traceable back to the document it came from. Harvey works with 150+ asset management firms and analyzes 178M+ documents each month; the Finance Engineering team is how that capability meets the way deal teams actually work.

Finance Engineers understand how investors think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live deal pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what investment teams actually need. It's a team built to make Harvey the platform investment teams can trust with their most important work.

This role is the first Finance Engineer dedicated to private credit. You will build the credit playbook — demo library, workflow templates, use cases — while running live pilots, and lead the credit practice as the team grows.

You may be asked to travel around 2–3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1–3 days at a time.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

Forward Deployed Finance Engineers on the private credit team are former credit investors who left the desk to help build the future of how credit gets underwritten. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with direct lenders, opportunistic and specialty finance managers, BDC managers, and insurer credit arms throughout the pre-sales process and stay with them well past it — leading pilots on live opportunities, guiding lenders through what's possible with AI, and sitting down with credit teams to build screening, underwriting, and credit committee workflows in the firm's own templates and formats.

The work is the work they did on the desk: lender presentation and CIM review; QoE read-throughs and data pack analysis; cash flow and leverage modeling; sizing and structuring; covenant and credit agreement review; credit memo drafting; and comps. It continues post-close into compliance certificate review, covenant tracking, amendment and waiver analysis, and quarterly portfolio reporting, so value compounds after the first deal. Along the way, Finance Engineers bring credit-team feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.







WHAT YOU HAVE




 - 6+ years on the investment or underwriting team at a direct lender, private credit fund, BDC manager, or insurer private credit arm, with demonstrated ownership of live deal work: screening, underwriting, diligence workstreams, modeling, structuring, and drafting credit committee materials. Asset-based and specialty finance backgrounds are welcome. Leveraged finance, restructuring advisory, or rating-agency experience before the principal side is welcome, but principal-side deal execution is required.

 - Strong command of the documents and data that drive a credit decision — lender presentation and CIM, QoE and data pack, model, credit agreement and intercreditor, compliance certificates — and an instinct for where the numbers and the paper disagree.

 - Advanced Excel and financial modeling, comfort with prompting and agentic AI workflows, and a builder's instinct for turning a repeated manual process into a repeatable automation. Python, SQL, or experience building internal tools is a plus.

 - Executive presence and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility from analysts and associates through to partners and credit committee members.

 - Outstanding communication and presentation skills — comfortable leading a live demo, facilitating a workshop, or holding your own in a technical conversation about a covenant package or an underwriting assumption.

 - Deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform investment work, paired with a practical, solutions-oriented mindset and bias toward action.

 - Track record partnering with senior stakeholders to drive results, with curiosity for testing approaches and optimizing for customer outcomes.

 - Customer-facing or commercial experience (LP or investor relations, capital formation, banking coverage, business development) and/or hands-on experience using AI tools in an investment setting are pluses.

Harvey is building a legal transformation practice for the AI era. Our Transformation Office brings together highly experienced consultants and practitioners to help law firms and legal departments turn AI from a tool their teams use into value their business can see.

Harvey’s experts help leaders decide what to change, and how to change it, as they adopt and embed new ways of working: how legal work is organized and governed, how it’s priced by firms and valued by in-house teams and how their people build new capability. Our advice draws on what we see across Harvey's customers in more than 50 countries and on where the technology is heading. Our client work shapes Harvey's product, and the product shapes our advice. Law firms and legal departments are making decisions now that will shape how they compete for the next decade: which work to prioritize, how to price and value it, how to staff it and how to organize around AI. jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Data Lifecycle
jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Team

Data Lifecycle at Decagon builds the systems that govern how sensitive customer data is handled throughout its lifetime: what we store, who can access it, how we redact it, and when we delete it. We turn complex privacy requirements into reliable infrastructure and product that customers can configure and trust.

This team is core to how Decagon scales. Our AI agents work with sensitive information across conversations, tool calls, and customer systems. The frameworks we build need to protect that data consistently across the platform, while preserving the context customers need to operate and improve their agents. A failure mode we debug in production becomes a guardrail, a test, or a piece of tooling that catches it everywhere.

Our systems run for companies like Hertz, American Airlines, and Notion across chat, voice, email, and SMS.



About the Role

You’ll design and build the platform infrastructure that let customers control how their data is collected, retained, redacted, and deleted. That means strong engineering underneath, and clear abstractions on top that hold up across different enterprise requirements without forking per customer.

You’ll work day to day with product management, governance, and security: understanding customer requirements, defining data handling guarantees, reviewing designs, and iterating through launch. You’ll stay close enough to customers to understand their privacy and operational needs in depth and to ensure what you’re building is actually right for them.

Engineers here own features end to end, from technical architecture through deployment and the iteration after it. On this team, that includes verifying that sensitive data is protected and the action actually completes. An understanding of durable and fault-tolerant systems is key.



In this role, you will

 - Build PII handling and redaction systems that identify and protect sensitive information across conversations, agent traces, and other customer data

 - Design configuration abstractions for redaction and retention policies that balance enterprise flexibility with clear, safe defaults

 - Build reliable data deletion workflows that propagate across storage systems and derived data, with retries, verification, and visibility into failures

 - Build self-serve tools and APIs that let customers configure, test, and understand their data lifecycle policies without relying on an engineer

 - Build LLM-backed systems that scan and detect data anomalies and violations

 - Train and/or tune models for detecting data of various forms (including PII and PHI)

 - Extend redaction and identification to multimodal agents, including images, attachments, voice notes, and documents.

 - Build monitoring and auditability that make it clear what data was processed, what remains, and where a policy has failed—without exposing sensitive information in the process

 - Handle data lifecycle systems at scale, including backfills, partial failures, and safe rollouts; your work will touch critical flows for Fortune 100 companies
   
   

Your background and skillset look something like this

 - 4+ years building software products, with strong product thinking

 - Proficient in Python, comfortable working across the entire stack

 - Experience designing reliable backend systems and data pipelines, including asynchronous processing, retries, and failure recovery

 - Understanding of what operational maturity looks like for critical systems, including observability and monitoring

 - Complex systems instincts: you can reason about where data flows, where copies persist, and what happens when one part of a workflow fails

 - A high degree of comfort debugging system failures in deep technology stacks, using whatever tool gets you to the answer

 - Judgment about when to ship fast and when correctness, privacy, and irreversible operations require slowing down
   
   

Even better

 - Experience with PII detection, redaction, tokenization, or secure handling of sensitive data

 - Experience building data retention, deletion, or privacy request workflows across multiple storage systems

 - Experience building security-sensitive product systems, such as authentication, authorization, and data access controls

 - Familiarity with privacy and compliance requirements such as GDPR, CCPA, or PCI, and translating them into engineering controls

 - Background with LLMs, evals, or AI agent systems, especially handling sensitive data in model inputs, outputs, and traces

 - Experience with observability, audit trails, or operational tooling for large-scale data systems

 - Work with sensitive data in voice, images, or other non-text formats



Compensation

$200K – $400K + Offers Equity



This range reflects the expected compensation for this role. Compensation within the range is determined based on experience, skills, and the scope of responsibilities, with flexibility for candidates who demonstrate exceptional impact. 



In addition to base salary, we offer competitive equity. Final compensation may vary based on location within the United States.



Benefits

We proudly offer the following benefits for our full-time employees:

 - Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life Insurance and Disability Benefits

 - Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K, pension)

 - Parental Leave

 - Monthly stipend to support your wellness, lifestyle, and work-life balance

 - Daily lunches and snacks in the office to keep you at your best

 - Take what you need vacation policy (subject to local requirements; UK employees receive 25 days of statutory leave)

These benefits are described in more detail in Decagon’s policies, may vary by location, and can change at any time according to applicable compensation and benefits plans.

jobs.description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Technical Product Marketing Manager who can pick up any Baseten product and explain it clearly to the people who buy it. Baseten sells dedicated inference, Model APIs, training and post-training, and the enterprise platform that ties them together. The work behind each one is the same: understand how the product works, know where it stands against the alternatives, and write about it well enough that an ML engineer trusts it and a buyer acts on it.

We’re hiring for this role across multiple product lines. You’ll work on whichever launch, narrative, or competitive gap matters most at the time, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and the rest of product marketing. It’s a good fit for someone who ramps on technical products quickly and wants to be the person who figures out the story.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Positioning & Technical Narrative

 - Own positioning and messaging for Baseten products across inference, Model APIs, training and post-training, and the core platform, written for ML engineers, platform teams, and executive buyers.

 - Work closely with Product and Engineering to understand architecture, tradeoffs, and roadmap, and make sure every technical claim is accurate and backed by how the product actually behaves.

 - Keep product-level messaging consistent with Baseten’s platform narrative so each product story supports the others.

 - Write messaging that is technically credible without getting lost in implementation detail.

Launches & Go-to-Market

 - Build and run launch plans for new products and major capabilities, from internal enablement through external announcement.

 - Decide what deserves a full launch and what should ship through docs, sales enablement, or targeted customer outreach.

 - Create launch assets including messaging briefs, landing pages, technical blog posts, demo storylines, sales decks, one-pagers, and FAQs.

 - Partner with Demand Gen, Sales, Solutions, and Customer Marketing to turn product capabilities into campaigns and deal support.

Competitive & Market Insight

 - Track the competitive landscape across inference providers, model API companies, hyperscalers, and internal DIY platforms, including pricing, packaging, launches, and messaging.

 - Turn that analysis into a clear point of view on where Baseten wins and loses, and use it to sharpen positioning.

 - Talk to customers and sellers to understand buying criteria, objections, and deal blockers, and bring what you learn back to Product and Marketing as concrete recommendations.

Sales Enablement

 - Build battlecards, competitive talk tracks, objection-handling guides, and product training that sellers actually use.

 - Work with Sales and Solutions to find enablement gaps and close them.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in product marketing, technical marketing, or developer marketing, with at least 2 of those years marketing to developers or technical buyers at an infrastructure, developer tools, cloud, data, or AI company.

 - Strong writing. You can take a dense technical topic and make it clear without oversimplifying it, and you have samples to show.

 - Technical fluency. You’re comfortable reading docs, asking engineers specific questions, and getting up to speed on concepts like inference, autoscaling, fine-tuning, and open- vs. closed-weight models.

 - Hands-on competitive analysis experience: you’ve compared products in depth, formed a view, and used it to change positioning, messaging, or how a deal was sold.

 - A track record of learning unfamiliar products and markets quickly and moving between them.

 - Experience launching technical products or capabilities, including deciding what to launch and how.

 - Comfortable owning both strategy and execution: landing pages, decks, one-pagers, and written content, not just frameworks.

 - Experience at a fast-moving startup, working with multiple stakeholders and shifting priorities.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, inference, model serving, or model training and post-training.

 - Experience marketing to ML engineers, platform engineers, infrastructure leaders, or technical executives.

 - Experience building competitive positioning against cloud providers, inference providers, model API companies, or internal platforms.

 - Time in an adjacent role such as solutions engineering, product management, developer relations, technical writing, or industry or equity research covering AI or infrastructure.





BENEFITS

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
We are an AI company operating at the cutting edge of the industry, growing quickly in a fast-moving environment. As we scale and prepare for a future IPO, we are building our Procurement function from the ground up. This is our first Procurement Analyst role in the company, so you will help define how we buy, not just execute it. Your passion for Procurement will help build and run our source-to-pay processes with strong internal controls, clear segregation of duties between procurement and payment, and audit-ready documentation. This is a global role: you will support stakeholders and suppliers across regions and work closely with the rest of the Procure to Pay (P2P) and Finance teams.
 Key Responsibilities
 Procurement operations
 Manage the end-to-end purchasing operations across all spend categories (software, cloud, professional services, hardware, facilities, and more), from requisition intake and PO issuance in Zip / Coupa.
 Review purchase requests for completeness, budget and policy compliance before approval.
 Issue and track purchase orders, and follow up with suppliers on delivery, pricing, and service levels.
 Support RFQ/RFP processes: gather requirements, solicit/compare bids, and document selection rationale.  Support negotiations and renewals in partnership with Legal and business owners.
 Support requesters across time zones and regions, handling multi-currency and cross-border purchasing needs.
 Controls and audit readiness
 Help design and implement procurement policies, approval matrices (delegation of authority), and procedures aligned with IPO and audit requirements.
 Enforce segregation of duties between procurement (requisition, sourcing, PO creation, vendor selection) and payment (invoice processing, payment execution), in coordination with Accounts Payable and Finance.
 Maintain complete, organized documentation for every purchase (quotes, approvals, contracts, POs) so it is available for internal and external audits.
 Monitor and report on policy exceptions, such as off-contract spend, retroactive POs, and split purchases, and escalate as needed.
 Support internal and external audit requests and help remediate findings.
 Vendor management
 Maintain accurate vendor master data and a centralized vendor and contract repository.
 Run supplier onboarding, including due diligence, documentation, tax compliance validation, and conflict-of-interest checks for domestic and international suppliers.
 Track supplier performance and support periodic vendor reviews using AI and other tools.
 Analysis and reporting
 Use AI to analyze spend data across categories and regions to identify savings opportunities, consolidation potential, and compliance gaps.
 Build regular reports and KPIs, such as spend under management, PO compliance, cycle times, and savings.
 Support budget tracking with Finance and flag potential overruns.
 Process improvement
 Contribute to the implementation and optimization of procurement tools and workflows, particularly Coupa and Zip.
 Document processes and create guidance and training for internal requesters.
 Propose and drive improvements that balance speed with control in a high-growth environment.
 Requirements
 Experience and knowledge
 3+ years of experience in Procurement, Purchasing, or a related P2P function.
 Hands-on experience with Coupa and Zip or other modern procurement and AP tools.
 Familiarity with corporate procurement policies, guidelines, and internal controls.
 Understanding of P2P cycle and basic concepts of segregation of duties and approval workflows.
 Professional fluency in English (written and spoken), as you will primarily support global teams and suppliers.
 Core competencies (non-negotiable)
 Interpersonal skills: builds trusted relationships with stakeholders at all levels and can say “no” or “not like this” constructively.  Strong negotiation and influencing skills.
 Communication skills: communicate clearly, in English writing and verbally, with business teams, suppliers, and senior leaders, and can explain the “why” behind controls.
 Ownership and a bias for action in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment.
 Strong attention to detail and a commitment to compliance and integrity.
 Self-management and strong written communication in a remote, cross-time-zone setting.
 Nice to have
 Experience in a high-growth, technology, or SaaS/AI company.
 Exposure to SOX, IPO readiness, or audit-ready environments.
 Familiarity with international supplier onboarding and tax documentation (e.g., W-8/W-9, VAT), and knowledge of EU, Mexican (CFDI, SAT compliance) as well as other government’s requirements.
 Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

 Procurement policy and approval matrix adopted and followed by the business.

 A centralized, audit-ready record for all purchases and vendors.
 Improved PO compliance and visibility into company spend.

 What you'll do
 Work with the UK Public Sector Lead, UK leadership, government relations and the wider team on go-to-market strategy across central government, defence & security, and enterprise

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Pricing Science
jobs.description:
Pricing is one of the most consequential decisions Amazon makes, and the science behind it needs to be causally rigorous, not just predictive. The P2 Optimization Science team builds the machine learning (ML) systems that power Amazon's pricing decisions at scale: demand lift models, customer lifetime value (LTV) frameworks, and the experimentation infrastructure that validates whether pricing changes actually work.
We're looking for a Research Scientist to own causal inference at the intersection of ML and pricing experimentation. Our team has identified a real gap: the methodological bridge between econometric analysis and production-scale ML pipelines needs a practitioner who lives in both worlds. You'll build conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation models, design analysis workflows for pricing experiments, and develop reusable causal ML infrastructure that the broader team — including non-ML scientists — can rely on. If you're a scientist who wants to tackle hard causal identification problems in a high-stakes production environment, and who finds satisfaction in making rigorous methods accessible to a broader team, this role is for you.
Key job responsibilities
- Design, train, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end causal ML pipelines for pricing use cases, including CATE estimation models and heterogeneous treatment effect frameworks.
- Serve as the team's causal ML methodology expert — defining identification strategies, model selection criteria, evaluation standards, and the tradeoffs between econometric and ML approaches to causal estimation.
- Contribute causal analysis methodology to pricing A/B test post-analysis and build reusable tooling that economists and other non-ML scientists can adopt without requiring deep ML expertise.
- Assess emerging causal inference methods (e.g., synthetic difference-in-differences, generalized random forests, causal representation learning) for applicability to Amazon's pricing context, and author internal methodology proposals for adoption.
- Partner with senior economists on identification strategy and causal assumptions, collaborate with software and data engineering partners on production deployment, and align with product managers on experiment design requirements.
A day in the life
Your work directly shapes the prices customers see on hundreds of millions of Amazon products. In a given week you might investigate an optimization anomaly in simulation and trace it to an unmodeled market dynamic, then design an offline evaluation framework to benchmark competing approaches before committing to online testing. You'll collaborate with senior economists on identification strategy for a pricing experiment, present a science proposal for incorporating a new competitiveness signal into an optimization system, or work with the experimentation platform team on randomization design. You'll also have opportunities to write up novel scientific findings for submission to venues such as KDD, NeurIPS, or the ACM Conference on Economics and Computation.
About the team
The P2 Optimization Science team sits at the center of Amazon's pricing decisions. We build the ML systems, causal inference pipelines, and experimentation infrastructure that determine how prices are set across Amazon's global catalog. Our team brings together research scientists, economists, and engineers who collaborate closely to turn rigorous methodology into production-quality systems with measurable business impact. We value scientific rigor, clear communication across disciplines, and a culture where every team member's work is designed to be extensible and useful beyond their own project. If you want your science to directly influence how hundreds of millions of customers experience Amazon, this is the team to join. - PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of quantitative field research experience
- Experience investigating the feasibility of applying scientific principles and concepts to business problems and products
- Experience analyzing both experimental and observational data sets - Knowledge of R, MATLAB, Python or similar scripting language
- Experience with agile development
- Experience building web based dashboards using common frameworks
- In depth familiarity with the literature and practice of operations management, supply chain management, inventory management, revenue management, forecasting, and/or logistics
- Prior well-established recognized academic experience, multiple publications in top-tier academic journals Programming experience using at least one modern programming language such as Python, Java, or C++
- Proficiency in model development, model validation and model implementation for large-scale applications
- Experience with developing prototypes by manipulating and analyzing complex, high-volume, high-dimensionality data from varying sources

We are looking for a Senior Manager of Package Signal & Power Integrity to lead a small team of engineers delivering SI/PI solutions for next-generation 2.5D/3D chiplet-based products. This is a player-coach role: you will set the technical direction for package-level SI/PI across advanced packaging platforms (CoWoS, EMIB, 3D die stacking) while staying hands-on with modeling, simulation, and post-silicon correlation.
You will own the SI/PI strategy from early architecture through high-volume production, partnering with silicon design, physical design, system architecture, and possible with OSAT/substrate vendors to ensure robust signaling and power delivery across die-to-die, memory, and high-speed SerDes interfaces.
What You Will Do

• Define and execute SI/PI design methodology for 2.5D/3D IC packages—including silicon interposer, RDL, TSV, and bridge-based architectures.
• Drive chip-package-system co-design by performing end-to-end SI/PI analysis and optimization for HBM (HBM3/HBM3E+), PCIe Gen5/Gen6/Gen7, UCIe die-to-die interconnects and high-speed SerDes (112G+/224G PAM4).
• Own PDN design and sign-off across die, interposer, package substrate, and PCB, including AC/DC/transient droop analysis and decoupling strategy.

• Partner with ASIC architects, PHY/IP teams, package layout, thermal/mechanical, PCB, and system design teams to close electrical specifications.

Required Qualifications
• MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering, with emphasis in electromagnetics, signal integrity, power integrity, or microelectronics.
• 12+ years of progressive SI/PI engineering experience in semiconductor packaging (IC package, interposer, or substrate design).

You will manage the store, data model, and query path, converting large streams of profiling and telemetry data into useful information for engineers and automated analysis.

 Develop and construct the store, data model, and query path for engineering performance data. This includes ingesting, joining, storing, and delivering it at the scale of a GPU data center with low latency.

 Take responsibility for the data contract with the teams that generate the data: establish it, version it, and transition consumers through changes without disrupting them. 
 Make deliberate trade-offs among data quality, query latency, storage cost, and retention, and verify improvements in efficiency, latency, and resource use with measurements. 
 Handle delayed, duplicated, incomplete, or inconsistent data, and make its limitations visible to downstream users. 
 Develop the data API along with the generated evidence views for people and automated analysis to access results. Implement access controls, resource limits, and maintain stable behavior during high demand or failures. 
 What we need to see: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 
 12+ years of relevant software engineering experience, including delivery and operation of data pipelines, storage systems, analytical services, or comparable software used by others. 
 Experience handling large-scale data in production, including billions of events per day or petabyte-class stores. Also experienced with low-latency streaming pipelines that manage backpressure, replay, and duplicate delivery accurately. 
 Good judgment about event identity and ordering, data transformations, and how errors or missing data affect results. 
 A concrete performance investigation you can explain: the baseline, measurements, competing explanations, change made, and verified result, including trade-offs. 
 Experience establishing and versioning a data contract with a producing team, and guiding consumers through a format change. 
 Ability to debug across component boundaries and validate changes through code review, tests, and independent measurements, including when using automated development tools. 
 Clear communication about choices in building, observed behavior, and uncertainty, with care for users’ data and operational constraints. 
 Proficiency with C++, Python, and SQL. 
 Ways to stand out from the crowd: 
 Hands-on work with telemetry, time-series data, or analytical query engines such as ClickHouse, and with columnar formats such as Arrow and Parquet. 
 Familiarity with profiler data: trace record formats, sampling semantics, symbolization, clock domains, and aligning events recorded on different machines. 
 High-cardinality schema build, and measured improvements to memory use, storage efficiency, or query performance while preserving correctness. 
 A track record of making data processing easier to inspect and recover when inputs change, traffic spikes, or failures occur. 
 Working knowledge of Go.
