jobs.description:
SLSQ327R374
 Databricks is seeking a  Lakebase Sales Specialist Account Executive in Japan to help customers modernize their operational data foundation with  Databricks Lakebase , our  fully-managed Postgres  offering for  intelligent applications . This high-impact role sits within the Lakebase Go-To-Market team and partners closely with regional Account Executives to drive adoption of Lakebase with platform, application, and data teams.
 Lakebase gives customers a unified, governed foundation for  operational workloads  and  AI-native applications , helping them move away from a fragmented estate of point databases toward a modern, scalable, serverless Postgres service. If you want to be at the forefront of operational databases for AI and intelligent applications at one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world, this is your opportunity.
 The impact you will have 
 Drive new Lakebase revenue  by identifying, qualifying, and closing Lakebase opportunities within a defined territory, in partnership with regional Account Executives and the broader account team.
 Lead with outcomes  for key Lakebase personas — including  platform teams and developers ,  data teams , and  central IT  — articulating how Lakebase helps them ship features faster, simplify operational data architectures, and improve governance and cost efficiency.
 Sell the value of fully-managed Postgres for intelligent applications , positioning Lakebase as the optimal choice for operational workloads that power real-time, AI-driven experiences.
 Run complex, multi-threaded sales cycles  from discovery and value hypothesis through commercial negotiation and close, navigating executive, technical, and line-of-business stakeholders.
 Orchestrate proof-of-value and POCs  that validate Lakebase’s benefits for OLTP-style workloads, reverse ETL, and AI/ML-driven applications, in partnership with solution architects and specialists.
 Compete and win  against legacy and cloud-native operational databases by leveraging our compete assets, benchmarks, and customer references.
 Align to measurable business outcomes  such as performance, developer productivity, time-to-market for new features, cost reduction, and simplification of the operational data landscape.
 Partner cross-functionally  with Product Management, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partner teams to shape territory plans, launch plays, and co-selling motions with key ISVs and GSIs.
 Enable the field  by sharing Lakebase best practices, success stories, and sales motions with broader sales teams, helping scale Lakebase proficiency across the organization.
 What success looks like in this role 
 This role requires the ability to operate across  two key motions  simultaneously:
 Establish top strategic focus accounts  by engaging application development teams to create net-new intelligent applications leveraging Lakebase.
 Drive longer-term Postgres standardization and migration  within Databricks' most strategic accounts.
 Candidates should demonstrate how they can  act as a force multiplier  across multiple dimensions of the business.
 Success in this role requires strength in four areas:
 Business ownership  – Operate at a business-unit level by tracking revenue, pipeline, and key observations, and by identifying areas needing additional focus or support.
 Strategic account engagement  – Partner with account teams to engage priority accounts across the global DB700, driving strategic opportunities from initial engagement through successful outcomes.
 Field enablement  – Build and execute enablement plans that empower AEs and SAs to confidently carry the Lakebase conversation even when the specialist is not present.
 Market voice and thought leadership  – Develop an internal and external presence by contributing to global AMAs and internal forums, and by representing Databricks at key first- and third-party events.
 The interview process is designed to evaluate candidates across all four of these dimensions.
 What we look for 
 7+ years of enterprise SaaS sales experience , consistently exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder deals.
 Proven success selling  data platforms, operational databases (e.g., Postgres, MySQL, cloud-native DBaaS), or adjacent data/AI infrastructure  to technical buyers and business leaders.
 Strong understanding of  modern data and application architectures , including cloud-native services, microservices, event-driven systems, and how operational data underpins AI and analytics strategies.
 Ability to sell to both  technical stakeholders  (developers, architects, data engineers) and  business stakeholders  (product leaders, operations, line-of-business owners).
 Demonstrated experience leading  specialist or overlay motions , working jointly with core Account Executives to create and progress opportunities.
 Executive presence with the ability to  whiteboard architectures , lead C-level conversations, and build trust with senior decision makers.
 Strong  value selling  skills: adept at discovering pain, building a business case, and tying technical capabilities to clear, quantified outcomes.
 Excellent  communication, storytelling, and negotiation  skills, with comfort presenting to both large and small audiences.
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience selling  Postgres, operational databases, OLTP workloads, or transactional cloud database services , ideally within large or strategic accounts.
 Familiarity with  data platforms, lakehouse architectures, and cloud ecosystems  (AWS, Azure, GCP), including how operational databases fit within broader data and AI strategies.
 Understanding of  reverse ETL, real-time decisioning, and operational analytics  use cases, and how they drive value for customer-facing and internal applications.
 Exposure to  AI-native and agent-driven applications  that depend on low-latency, highly scalable operational data services.
 Prior experience in a  high-growth, category-creating environment , helping shape new plays, messaging, and customer narratives.
 Experience collaborating with  partners and ISVs  to drive joint pipeline and co-sell motions.

 You will report to the VP & Associate General Counsel, Strategic Alliances & Integration 
 Strategic partnerships are an essential pillar to Databricks' providing the world's leading data & AI platform, integrating the broadest range of the latest leading technologies from proven partner providers. In this role, you will work closely with Databricks Strategic Alliances and cross-functional stakeholders, orchestrating advice and contributions across internal and external experts, and innovating to provide solutions in a rapidly evolving landscape.

You must be an agile, resourceful self-starter, comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, and excellent at building strong relationships and giving clear, pragmatic advice.  You have a bias for action, enjoy building, thrive on finding creative solutions to new challenges, and value seeing your direct impact on the business.

 Drive or provide legal support for other strategic transactions or projects, including collaborating in developing new partnering motions, and developing new processes and templates to scale our strategic partner practice

 You have at least 10 years of experience at a nationally recognized law firm and / or in-house legal department at a high-tech company

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure
jobs.description:
GAQ327R264 
 At Databricks Information Technology, we are a product-led organization transforming the way we work, from how easy it is to use our IT services to the applications we develop to help us scale seamlessly amid incredible growth.
 As a Software Engineer, Infrastructure , you will be a core technical contributor on the IT CorpEng Infrastructure team, owning and driving the evolution of our core infrastructure and observability platforms. This role requires a strong software engineering mindset, deep technical breadth across SRE and infrastructure worlds, and the ability to deliver high-quality, scalable solutions for currently "immature" system problems. You will be responsible for building resilient, scalable, and automated infrastructure that empowers our development teams. As a member of the team, you will bridge the gap between software engineering and systems architecture, ensuring our AWS environment is cost-optimized, secure, and highly available.
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Automate: Develop and deploy production-grade infrastructure on cloud platforms (AWS preferred) using Infrastructure as Code tools like Terraform or Pulumi.
 Orchestration: Deploy, manage, and scale containerized workloads using Kubernetes (EKS/AKS), focusing on security, reliability, and resource efficiency.
 CI/CD Excellence: Build and maintain robust deployment pipelines using GitHub Actions, including both cloud-hosted and self-hosted runners for specialized build requirements.
 Drive "Observable by Default" Frameworks: Implement infrastructure standards to ensure new internal applications are secure, with logging, metrics, and tracing configured out of the box.
 Tooling, Scripting & AI: Build internal CLI tools, AI-assisted workflows, and automation scripts to streamline developer workflows and reduce manual toil.
 Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate with Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, and Support teams to execute technical projects aligned with business outcomes.
 Document & Knowledge Share: Participate in peer code reviews, maintain operational playbooks/failure triage guides, and help onboard team members onto platforms you maintain.
 What We Look For 
 Software Engineering Expertise: 3+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python for scripting, automation, and tooling (required).
 Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Solid working knowledge of Terraform (modules, state management) or Pulumi (preferred).
 Cloud & Containerization: Hands-on experience building and supporting production workloads in AWS (or Azure/GCP), along with Kubernetes and Docker fundamentals.
 CI/CD & Automation: Practical experience designing, maintaining, and troubleshooting pipelines using GitHub Actions or similar modern CI/CD tools.
 Observability Foundations: Practical understanding of observability pillars (logging, metrics, tracing) and hands-on experience integrating tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana.
 Independent Execution: Proven ability to own end-to-end tasks with guidance from Tech Leads, breaking down broader technical goals into actionable technical solutions.

jobs.description:
GAQ128R84
 Databricks is seeking a Senior Product Counsel to help the Databricks legal team provide cutting-edge, practical legal advice to Databricks’ engineering and product management teams as we navigate rapidly evolving global laws and regulations in big data, including data privacy, data protection, and AI.  This role will report to the Assistant General Counsel, Product. 
 The impact you will have: 
 Demonstrate expertise in product counseling, data protection laws, marketing, and technology transactions, as well as the capacity to be a generalist and learn new areas of law and legal skills quickly. 
 Exercise keen business and legal judgment. You know when to say “yes”, “no, unless …”, and “no”, but you also know when to escalate concerns. 
 Contribute to developing processes to improve our product counseling function.
 Provide end-to-end product counseling - from ideation to end of life.
 Partner with teams across Databricks and close external partners that are building, deploying, and operating technology for external and internal users. 
 Work cross-functionally with the commercialization, product marketing, marketing, and communications teams to bring our transformative offerings to market. 
 Collaborate with other legal leaders in commercial, go-to-market, compliance, corporate, and public affairs with respect to product issues.
 Deeply understand product and data risk issues to be able to hear and answer questions that aren’t asked and translate technical and security concerns into answers understandable to non-technical lawyers. 
 Assist your product stakeholders in developing process improvements.
 Draft and update form agreements regarding products and services, and negotiate product and security-related changes to customer contracts, including those in DPAs and BAAs.
 Provide general legal support on a flexible, as-needed basis with respect to other areas of the business.
 Work with potential vendors to understand data flows to determine privacy and data protection risk, and coordinate with the privacy legal team as appropriate. 
 Advise on cybersecurity issues as a member of incident response teams.
 Contribute as a team player to further the legal department's reputation as an effective, respected, and valued resource within the company.
 What we look for: 
 8+ years of relevant legal experience at a top law firm and/or in-house (a combination of both is a plus), with a minimum of 2 years focused experience in product, privacy, and/or IP law 
 Experience with AI, FedRAMP requirements, or payments a plus
 Experience working for a company offering platform services to business customers is a plus
 Deep understanding of cloud and software technology, and a strong desire to work on legal issues in these areas

jobs.title: Sr. Sales Compensation Analyst
jobs.description:
GAQ128R88
 As a Sr. Sales Compensation Analyst on the Comp Admin team, you will run commissions administration from start to finish for a large global group of sellers, so they can trust that they are paid accurately and on time. You will own a large payee portfolio with no supervision needed, from plan rollout through calculation, payroll, and follow-up support. You will catch issues before they reach the field and keep every step audit-ready. You will also use AI and automation every day to make our work faster, more accurate, and easier to scale as Databricks grows.
 The impact you will have: 
 Own commissions administration for a large payee portfolio with no errors: user setup, plan distribution, input processing, calculation, and payment.
 Deliver plan rollout and payout accurately and on time every cycle, including tracking ICPW acceptance and preparing data that feeds payroll and accounting deadlines.
 Resolve payee and partner questions quickly and fully, so issues are settled the first time without escalations. Run rep training and enablement sessions as needed.
 Keep your portfolio fully compliant with SOX and audit requirements by following controls with discipline, documenting clearly, and keeping evidence reproducible.
 Find discrepancies, exceptions, and control gaps early (for example, wrong credits, quota mismatches, or cap and accelerator errors), trace the root cause in the data, and drive the fix with Sales Ops, Payroll, and Accounting.
 Make recurring workflows faster, more reliable, and easier to repeat by improving documentation, simplifying handoffs, and cutting rework.
 Use AI to improve recurring work such as validations, reconciliations, and responses to comp questions. Build repeatable approaches that others on the team can adopt.
 Help the team grow by mentoring new hires on tools, processes, and best practices, and by referring strong candidates.
 What we look for: 
 5+ years of hands-on sales compensation administration, including user setup, plan distribution, calculation and payment, comp questions, and rep training.
 Advanced Xactly skills, including administration, reporting, and troubleshooting, with the ability to resolve system issues on your own.
 Advanced Excel and Google Workspace skills for complex modeling, data analysis, and reconciliation.
 A solid grasp of SaaS go-to-market compensation models (commit vs. consumption, quotas, OTI, accelerators, overlays, SPIFFs, MBOs) and how plan mechanics shape seller behavior.
 Experience working under SOX or similar audit controls, with accurate, well-documented work and clean audit trails.
 Strong analytical judgment: you investigate patterns, find root causes, and turn data into practical recommendations.
 Comfort using AI tools and LLMs in daily work, plus the judgment to check outputs for accuracy before relying on them.
 Clear communication and teamwork across time zones with global partners in Sales Ops, Payroll, Accounting, and Sales leadership.

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, CustomerLake (ML/LLM)
jobs.description:
P-1607
 At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best Data Intelligence Platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to tackle technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.
 As one of the first engineers in the NYC Engineering office, you'll join a small, nimble team building new products from the ground up. We're building CustomerLake, the Customer Data Platform on Databricks, to bring enterprise-grade ML and AI personalization to every company whose data already lives on Databricks. The best B2C and B2B brands have historically relied on in-house ML/AI teams to power personalization, recommendations, churn and lifetime-value modeling, and audience targeting. Our goal is to deliver that same capability to companies that don't have an in-house team but already have their data in order on Databricks. This is a true 0-to-1 environment, combining the excitement of a startup with the resources of a tech leader like Databricks.
 The impact you'll have: 
 Evaluate ML and LLM approaches for CustomerLake's personalization use cases, push the models and algorithms forward, and continuously improve quality over time
 Go deep on how models behave in production: inspect individual traces, understand how the models reason, and tune and improve from there
 Build the platform and evaluation framework that let CustomerLake customers optimize for real business value such as purchases, retention, and product usage, not vanity metrics like email opens and clicks
 Push the team toward new directions and novel methods worth tackling, not just optimizing what already exists
 Partner closely with product management, engineering, and design to turn ambiguous customer problems into scalable, trustworthy solutions
 Set the technical foundation and best practices for our ML/AI personalization work as we grow this into several roles across our products over the next 1-2 years
 What we look for: 
 10+ years of engineering experience, with a strong foundation across the full loop of shipping and improving ML/AI products
 Hands-on experience building and evaluating ML models and/or LLM systems for real product or business use cases; your understanding is practical, not purely academic, and you can make models work well inside a product
 Experience with personalization based on customer behavior (ideal) or transactions (acceptable), such as recommendations, targeting, churn, or lifetime-value modeling
 Proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch), with hands-on experience in model evaluation and monitoring AI quality in production
 Familiarity with LLMs and generative AI, including techniques like retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt design, fine-tuning, and evaluation
 A demonstrated product mindset, with the ability to translate ambiguous customer problems into scrappy MVPs and iterate quickly based on data and user feedback
 High ownership and bias for action in 0-to-1 environments: comfortable making pragmatic trade-offs, operating with incomplete information, and driving projects from idea through launch and adoption

 Experience in martech, ideally a go-to-market or business use case with an analytical (rather than purely transactional) angle

You thrive in a dynamic environment, are equally comfortable whiteboarding a medallion architecture with a data engineering team and presenting data ROI to a C-suite, and you bring deep opinions about what good data platform design looks like.

Location Requirement: Must be in North Carolina or South Carolina.




IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL GET TO:

 - Present Snowflake's Data Cloud vision to data engineering leaders, analytics teams, data scientists, and executive stakeholders at prospects and customers

 - Lead hands-on technical discovery to map a customer's existing data architecture — pipelines, warehouses, lakehouses, governance gaps — and design a Snowflake-native path forward

 - Build and deliver tailored demos and proof of concepts across Snowflake's full data platform: data engineering (Snowpark, Dynamic Tables, Snowpipe), AI/ML (Cortex AI, ML model registry), and data sharing (Data Clean Rooms, Marketplace listings)

 - Guide customers through modern data architecture patterns including Data Mesh, Data Lakehouse, real-time streaming pipelines, and unified governance frameworks

 - Translate ambiguous business problems — churn prediction, supply chain visibility, financial consolidation, operational analytics — into concrete Snowflake data solutions

 - Partner with Product Management, Engineering, and Field teams to feed customer data architecture patterns back into the product roadmap

 


ON DAY ONE WE WILL EXPECT YOU TO HAVE:

 - 3–8 years of industry experience, in a pre-sales or solutions architecture role focused on data platforms

 - Deep hands-on expertise with SQL, Python, and cloud data warehouse / data lakehouse architectures; able to write working code in a customer session without hesitation

 - Broad experience across the modern data stack: ETL/ELT tools (dbt, Fivetran, Informatica, Spark), streaming platforms (Kafka, Kinesis), orchestration (Airflow, dbt Cloud), BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Power BI), and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP)

 - Proven ability to conduct deep data architecture discovery — understanding a customer's source systems, transformation layers, consumption patterns, and governance requirements — and connect those findings to a Snowflake reference architecture

 - Experience positioning AI and ML capabilities within a data platform context: feature stores, model training pipelines, LLM-powered applications, and AI governance

 - Strong intuition for data governance, quality, and compliance challenges (GDPR, CCPA, PCI) and how platform design decisions affect them

 - Ability to quantify the business value of a modern data architecture — cost reduction, time-to-insight, pipeline reliability, data product monetization

 - A demonstrated track record using AI code generation tools to accelerate prototyping and proof-of-concept delivery

 - University degree in computer science, data science, engineering, mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. A Master's in Data Science or Business Analytics is a plus

 - Experience working with GSIs (EY, Deloitte, Accenture, Slalom, etc.) on large data platform programs is beneficial but not required

 


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

 - $220,000 - $288,000 OTE (On Target Earnings = Base Salary + Commission/Quota)

 - Snowflake offers competitive base salary, variable compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits including 401(k), health/dental/vision, flexible PTO, and professional development budget.

 


ABOUT OUR TEAM:

Our Solution Engineers are customer-obsessed data practitioners. We believe in rigorous discovery before prescribing solutions, we stay honest about what Snowflake can and can't do, and we hold ourselves accountable to outcomes — not just demos. We love to learn, give and receive direct feedback, and are relentless about making our customers' data more accessible, reliable, and valuable. If you have strong opinions about data architecture and enjoy proving them with working code, you'll fit right in.

 


ABOUT SNOWFLAKE:

Snowflake started with a clear vision: make modern data warehousing effective, affordable, and accessible to all data users. Today the Snowflake Data Cloud goes far beyond warehousing — it's where organizations build data pipelines, run ML workloads, share live data across the ecosystem, and power AI applications, all on a single governed platform. Our built-for-the-cloud architecture delivers the performance of a data warehouse, the flexibility of a data lake, and the elasticity of the cloud at a fraction of traditional costs.

jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

We are seeking a proactive, highly adaptable Senior Workplace Technician to be the full-time, on-site anchor (Mon–Fri) of our office campus. You are a natural self-starter who brings a warm approachable energy, a customer-first mindset and a sharp eye for the details that make a workplace feel exceptional. 
Beyond your technical and practical know-how, your greatest strength lies in taking complete ownership—stepping up in grey areas, adapting to quick pivots, and executing high-impact solutions with ease.



GENERAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

In this role, you will keep our daily office environment running smoothly by taking ownership of a diverse set of workplace and operational functions, including: 


 - Lead physical office modifications, move/add/change (MAC) activities, furniture assemblies, and spatial reconfigurations.

 - Skilled in both digital workplace platforms (Google Workspace, Slack, ticketing systems, space planning apps) and practical, hands-on physical execution like furniture assembly, basic repairs, and everyday maintenance.

 - Oversee campus EV charging stations by monitoring usage, troubleshooting technical issues on the spot, and partnering directly with vendors for hardware or software resolutions.

 - Operational Optimization: Stay three steps ahead by spotting bottlenecks early and bringing fresh, creative ideas to make our physical facilities run smarter and more efficiently.

 - Builds strong in-person relationships with cross-functional partners and team members to plan, coordinate, and deliver exceptional everyday workplace services.

 - Resolve facilities tickets efficiently and with care, keeping communication transparent and ensuring every workplace request is handled to the highest standard.

 - Manage project budgets efficiently: monitoring spend, driving cost-effective vendor solutions, and maintaining tight fiscal responsibility across all on-site initiatives.

 - Vendor Management: Manage on-site third-party vendors and contractors, ensuring service partners consistently meet standards of accountability and performance quality.

 - Experience: You’ve spent 5+ years in facility operations, managing multi-floor spaces or large corporate campuses where things move fast.  If you have trade certifications (IFMA, BOC, LEED AP, or similar), that's definitely a big plus in our book.

jobs.title: Senior Implementation Manager
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
Implementation is a critical moment in the customer journey: it's where clients first see VTS deliver the value  they bought, and where retention truly begins. In the Senior Implementation Manager role, you will guide global leaders in commercial real estate toward driving early, measurable value from VTS. You'll own onboarding for our largest, most sophisticated  clients, leading enterprise rollouts of VTS AI, from portfolio-scale document abstraction to persona-based activation. Effective Senior Implementation Managers set our clients up for immediate value and long-term retention from day one. This role is fully client facing and is equal parts onboarding and outcome realization. 
 **Please note that this opportunity is located in New York, NY, and requires this hire to work from our office four days a week.** 
 What you can expect as a Senior Implementation Manager: 
 This isn't your typical implementation role. At VTS, you'll join a lean, high-impact, AI-augmented implementation team that shares one mission with Client Success - deliver value to your client. 
 You will:
 Command the Onboarding: Own end-to-end onboarding for enterprise accounts, including scope, data readiness, configuration, enablement, and handoff, and run it with enough rigor that status, risk, and next steps are never in question.
 Build Trusted Partnerships Early: Establish trusted-advisor relationships with executive sponsors, asset managers, lease administrators, and senior decision-makers from kickoff, aligning every rollout to the business outcomes the client bought VTS to achieve.
 Drive Time-to-Adoption, Not Just Go-Live: VTS delivers value as soon as the data starts to flow into the platform. Move far beyond the deployment checklist. Onboarding and Outcomes continue to live side by side. Lead prescriptive, persona-based rollouts, run our adoption playbooks from the day of enablement, and use adoption signals, not task completion, to decide when an account is ready to transition to Client Success.
 Lead Change: Act as a change leader inside client organizations, proactively identifying workflow gaps and challenging clients when necessary so that VTS becomes how their teams actually work.
 Orchestrate Delivery Partners: Manage strategic relationships with third-party delivery partners, including our document abstraction partners. Hold them accountable to volume, quality, and timelines, and turn daily delivery data into clear priorities and escalations.
 Mitigate Implementation Risk: Use adoption data, delivery metrics, and modern tooling to spot at-risk rollouts early (delayed client data, low engagement, misaligned stakeholders) and deploy swift, cross-functional solutions before that risk reaches the renewal.
 Collaborate Within a Coordinated Ecosystem: Orchestrate Sales, Client Success, Support, Product, and Engineering through the implementation stage of the customer journey so clients experience one unified VTS team, ending in a clean, evidence-based handoff to their CSM.
 Be the Voice of the Customer: Channel product feedback, defects, and strategic client needs to Product and Engineering with the specificity needed to help shape the future of the VTS platform.
 Be a Problem Solver:  Raise the Bar for the Team: Help shape how VTS onboards enterprise clients by contributing to our playbooks, runbooks, and processes, and mentor fellow IMs as we scale new product rollouts. Be hands on with leveraging technology to solve your problems.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Low Level (C++)

As an engineer based out of our Singapore office, you will play a critical role in the process of establishing HRT's presence in Asia-Pacific markets and work closely with our algo and operations teams to ensure the continued success of our trading. You will also be deeply involved in the continuous, ongoing process of optimizing trading in markets HRT already has a presence in. 
 In this role, you'll be expected to own the process of entering new markets and manage market changes over time. With this responsibility, you'll gain broad exposure to both the technical and business aspects of our trading operation. It is difficult to overstate the impact of this role - you will immediately contribute to the bottom line as HRT begins trading in markets it previously had no presence in and HRT’s trading in existing markets becomes more profitable. 
 Profile 
 In your spare time you: code, tinker, read, explore, break things, and have an insatiable curiosity for all things computer related... you'll find like-minded people here.

 You really like to work with people who challenge you and make you better at what you do​

 Adept at working independently and in self-management

We embrace a culture of togetherness that extends far beyond the walls of our office.

jobs.title: Trade Network Architect
jobs.description:
Hudson River Trading (HRT) is seeking an Ultra-Low Latency Network Architect to build, test, and optimize our global high-frequency trading infrastructure. In this role, you will lead hardware evaluation and lab benchmarking while leveraging Python and data analysis techniques to analyze high-volume PCAP captures, telemetry streams, and tick-to-trade latency distributions. You will bridge low-level network engineering with performance engineering teams to reduce jitter and push network performance into the single nanosecond domain. 
 Responsibilities 
 Hardware Evaluation & Lab Testing: Establish and run a dedicated network testing lab. Design automated benchmark frameworks using traffic generators (Spirent/Ixia) to simulate, measure and validate various protocols at a network level and to stress-test  SmartNICs, switches, FPGAs, and transceivers
 Network Data Analysis & Telemetry Pipeline: Build custom Python pipelines to process, analyze, and visualize high-volume packet captures (PCAPs), queue depth metrics, and telemetry data from FPGA/Corvil appliances to pinpoint anomalies. Write tools to automate lab testing procedures, parse binary network logs, and generate latency-distribution reports (e.g., 99.99th percentile jitter analysis)
 HFT Architecture & Co-location: Architect and maintain low latency trading networks across global exchange colocation sites. Optimize trading network signals over wireless low-latency backhaul networks
 Kernel Bypass & Acceleration: Familiarity with kernel-bypass stacks (AMD/Solarflare Onload/DPDK), hardware accelerator cards and layer-1/2 FPGA switches to minimize execution overhead. Collaborate with hardware engineering teams to benchmark performance for embedded network components such as network adapters and/or network co-processors
 Time Synchronization: Oversee PTP (IEEE 1588v2) and White Rabbit time synchronisation systems
 Routing and Switching: Design and maintain large-scale L2/L3 architectures specifically fine-tuning BGP, OSPF and PIM-SSM/IGMP multicast trees for sub-microsecond convergence and resilient market data delivery
 Maintain Industry Awareness: Stay current with emerging low-latency networking technologies, including new SmartNICs, FPGA acceleration, and high-speed transceivers. Evaluate and recommend new hardware and software solutions to improve network performance
 Qualifications 
 10+ years designing and operating ultra-low latency networks within HFT, market making, or quantitative fund environments. Knowledge of exchange colocation, market data feeds, and order routing protocols (FIX, OUCH, ITCH) is essential
 Advanced Python skills using libraries like pandas, numpy, or pyarrow to parse large PCAP datasets, analyze time-series telemetry, and calculate microsecond/nanosecond statistics
 Hands-on experience building network testing labs, using hardware traffic generators (Spirent/Ixia) and packet capture tools
 Expertise with Arista (7130 series), Cisco (Nexus 3550/3548), LDA L1 switches, AMD Solarflare, and NVIDIA Mellanox hardware. Familiarity with FPGA driven low latency applications or custom accelerator cards  in the context of high performance trading environments
 Deep knowledge of BGP/OSPF, Linux network stack tuning, PTP (IEEE 1588), White Rabbit, PIM-SSM multicast, and large scale L2/L3 topologies. Awareness and experience with AI inference networks is a plus but not required

jobs.title: Senior Human Resources Business Partner
jobs.description:
About the role   
 The HR team helps protect the firm's largest investment: our people. As a Senior HRBP in our global People Operations team, you'll work with business leaders on complex organizational challenges as the business changes and help keep our culture strong along the way. A large part of the role is coaching. You'll be a trusted coach to leaders and managers, helping them lead their teams, handle hard moments and grow their people. The role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll care about the people, and you'll also see how a great workplace drives business results.   
 We work in a flat, consensus-driven environment where influence matters more than hierarchy. Our team is innovative, driven, collaborative and trustworthy, and we care about what we do and who we do it with.   
 What you'll do   
 Partner on people strategy. Be a thought partner to business leaders. Turn business strategy into decisions on workforce planning, org design, succession and talent. Help managers set their annual priorities and plans. 
 Coach leaders and managers.  Be a trusted one-to-one coach to senior leaders and people managers. Provide coaching on leadership style, performance and feedback conversations, team dynamics, stakeholder relationships and leading through change. Help leaders see their blind spots and build habits to address them. 
 Develop talent.  Help managers grow their people through development plans, internal moves and global career opportunities. Identify high-potential talent and support succession planning. 
 Build coaching capability across the firm.  Support first-time and newly promoted managers through the transition into leadership. Run coaching-based conversations and small-group sessions that grow management capability. Help build a culture where feedback and development happen continuously, not just at review time. 
 Lead employee relations.  Spot, reduce and resolve employee issues and conflict early, with sound judgment, discretion and fairness. Manage ER cases end to end, including grievances, investigations, performance and disciplinary matters, and sensitive exits, working closely with Legal. Coach managers to handle issues themselves where they can. 
 Drive engagement and retention.  Work out what's working and what isn't in the employee experience. Design practical fixes that strengthen engagement and keep critical talent, in line with our values. 
 Carry the culture.  Make sure team and people decisions reflect our core values, and challenge constructively when they don't. 
 Deliver core HR cycles.  Contribute to global processes including performance review, merit and bonus, global mobility, leave and offboarding. Bring the regional view and improve each cycle. 
 Connect regional and global.  Represent APAC needs within global People Operations. Share updates, good practice and new ideas, and help shape improvements to HR operations, systems and processes. 
 Manage risk and compliance.  Work with Legal, Compliance and senior management on local, regional and global changes. Ensure compliance with Hong Kong and wider APAC employment law, and with contract terms such as confidentiality, non-solicitation and non-compete. 
 Develop the HR team.  Mentor and coach HR colleagues and help raise the bar on how we deliver.   
 Other duties as assigned or needed. 
 What you'll bring   
 A proven record of coaching senior leaders and managers to change how they behave, not just giving advice. You can give specific examples of leaders you've helped grow. 
 Strong coaching skills. You listen actively to what is said and what isn't, you choose questions that open up or focus a conversation, and you can give direct, candid feedback in a way that lands. 
 The credibility and presence to challenge senior people constructively and be welcomed back. 
 Strong business acumen. You understand how the business works and can turn business problems into people solutions. 
 A track record of influencing senior stakeholders and building trust in a global matrix organization, including where you have no formal authority. 
 Comfort with ambiguity. You can solve problems where no process or system exists yet, and move quickly across distributed, cross-functional teams. 
 Adaptability with AI. You use AI tools in your daily work, adapt quickly as technology changes how HR works, and apply sound judgment on data privacy and confidentiality. 
 Calm, fair judgment in complex ER situations, and the ability to balance employee, business and legal risk. 
 Sound judgment and complete discretion with sensitive and confidential information. 
 Clear written and verbal communication, strong prioritization and close attention to detail. 
 Curiosity, empathy, and a strong wish to keep learning and to develop others. 
 An interest in building broad, cross-functional experience within People Operations. 
 A sense of humor.   
 Requirements   
 10+ years of progressive HR experience, with a large share of it as an HRBP. Financial services, technology or high-growth experience strongly preferred. 
 Substantial hands-on employee relations experience, including running workplace investigations, handling grievances, performance and disciplinary cases, and managing sensitive or negotiated exits, ideally including senior employees in Hong Kong and APAC. 
 Hands-on experience coaching senior leaders and people managers. A recognized coaching qualification (e.g. ICF-accredited) or formal training in coaching or psychometric tools is a strong plus. 
 Broad generalist depth across performance management, compensation, talent management and global mobility. 
 Solid working knowledge of Hong Kong employment law and practice, including the Employment Ordinance, MPF and PDPO. Experience across APAC (e.g. Mainland China, Singapore, Australia and India) a plus. 
 Experience with HRIS and recruiting systems (e.g. Workday, Greenhouse) and collaboration tools (e.g. Confluence, JIRA). 
 Bachelor's or higher degree in HR, Business, Psychology or a related field. 
 Fluent English. Mandarin and/or Cantonese a plus.   
 Reliable and predictable availability.

You will support sourcing activities, supplier negotiations, contract renewals and procurement operations while also helping us identify and implement improvements to our processes.    
 What you'll do  
 Sourcing & negotiation   
 Support sourcing initiatives across a range of non-technology categories, working with stakeholders to understand their requirements and identify appropriate suppliers and commercial solutions   
 Negotiate pricing and commercial terms with suppliers   
 Ensure that contracts meet our internal policies, risk standards and market benchmarks   
 Manage contract renewals for expiring agreements, engaging stakeholders and suppliers proactively to ensure continuity and favourable outcomes   
 Procurement operations

 Identify inefficiencies, gaps and opportunities to simplify or improve existing procurement processes

 Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with teams across the business   
 Confidence in negotiating with suppliers on pricing, commercial terms and contract renewals   
 A growth mindset with the ability to challenge existing processes and identify improvement opportunities   
 Solid organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to juggle shifting priorities 
 Who we are 
 At Optiver, our mission is to constantly improve the market by injecting liquidity, providing accurate pricing, increasing transparency and acting as a stabilizing force no matter the market conditions. With a focus on continuous improvement, we participate in the safeguarding of healthy and efficient markets for everyone who participates. As one of the largest market making institutions, we are a trusted partner of 70+ exchanges across the globe.

 You’ll join a culture of collaboration and excellence, where you’ll be surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem solvers. Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talented colleagues, working collectively to tackle the toughest problems in the financial markets.

 Training and continuous learning opportunities, including access to conferences and tech events.
 Competitive relocation packages and visa sponsorship where necessary for expats.

They opened the firm’s first office in 2011 in the heart of the derivatives industry and the options capital of the world – Chicago. Today, Akuna is proud to operate from additional offices in Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore and London.
 What you’ll do as a Quantitative Developer on the Quant Trading & Research team at Akuna: 
 Akuna’s Quantitative Trading and Research team creates trading strategies scientifically by combining its quantitative expertise with sophisticated understanding of derivatives and financial markets. The team is looking to add Quantitative Developers who will work alongside researchers, traders, and system engineers to develop software that incorporates vast amounts of data to drive sophisticated strategies, capturing market opportunities before our competition.
The successful candidate will have a strong programming background to produce trading solutions and high-performance production code. In this role you will:
 Design and develop production code of trading strategies: pricing models, execution logic and performance optimization
 Develop and improve data and research pipeline
 Advance existing codebase and propose new solutions and improvements
 Requirements for this role: 
 3+ years of experience developing performant, scalable applications in modern C++
 BS/MS/PhD degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Math, or equivalent
 Experience using data to drive decision-making
 Desire and ability to learn the intricacies of financial markets
 Willing to prepare and take English technical interviews 
 Qualities that make great candidates: 
 Solid understanding of multi-threaded/multi-core programming paradigms
 Experience with high frequency trading system
 Deeper understanding of any of the following fields: Linear Algebra, Numerical Methods, Statistics, Optimization, Signal Processing, Computer Architecture, Machine Learning, Heterogeneous/High Performance computing
 The ability to react quickly and accurately to rapidly changing market conditions, including the ability to quickly and accurately respond and/or solve math and coding problems are essential functions of the role
 Passion towards financial markets and trading

jobs.title: Fundamental Researcher
jobs.description:
ABOUT CANVAS
On our proprietary research team—Market Intelligence—you’ll partner with our Investment Professionals and Compliance team to uncover insights about companies, industries, and the broader economy through deep fundamental research.
Canvas is the supply chain research group within Market Intelligence. Canvas conducts compliant supply chain research by developing deep industry expertise, talking with private company executives, and synthesizing information for portfolio managers and analysts – our team produces impactful research that will change the way you look at the world.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
When you join the Canvas team, you’re signing up for the learning experience of your life. You will never look at anything the same – from grocery stores to tires to semiconductors. Every day you will speak with some of the most successful private company executives and learn about the businesses they’ve spent their lives building. You will synthesize your findings in comprehensive reports that are consumed by our investment professionals.
Other Market Intelligence divisions do quantitative research to explain what is going on in an industry. As a fundamental researcher, your qualitative research will explain the why. In this role you will:
• Become a subject matter expert on an assigned industry
• Learn from small, medium, and large private company executives about their businesses and the industries in which they operate, including gathering qualitative data on what is happening (e.g., structural shifts; real-time changes in supply/demand dynamics; and emerging competitors, markets, and technologies) and, importantly, why it is happening
• Synthesize your findings in comprehensive reports that present a view of the industry
• Gain unparalleled exposure to, and learn from, business leaders across industries, including private company executives and your colleagues
• Interact directly with our investment professionals and learn the discretionary investment process to help drive more informed investment decisions
 WHAT EXCITES YOU
• Staying current on the evolving alternative data market and its role in discretionary investing
• Speaking with experts both inside and outside the firm to understand data needs and offerings
• Analytical thinking and sifting through available data to find “the answer”
• Fast-paced work environments that at times require switching gears to address the needs of the business
• Working as part of a cross-functional team made up of investment, research, and compliance professionals
 WHAT EXCITES US
• Excellent attention to detail, organization, and project management skills
• Superb business intuition and a solution orientated, methodological approach to problem solving
• Ability to collaborate and build relationships across multiple business units within the Firm
• People who “elevate the room” through their work ethic, curiosity, and solution-orientated attitude
• Adherence to the highest ethical standards working closely with the firm’s Compliance team
 WHAT’S REQUIRED
• An undergraduate degree or advanced degree with demonstrated academic success
• Strong analytical skills
• Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
• An eagerness to find out if your conclusions are right or wrong
• An understanding of how companies work (their processes and outcomes) or an interest in learning
• Intellectual curiosity, creative thinking, maturity
• Highest standards of ethical decision making
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
• Integrity – You demonstrate 100% commitment to the highest ethical standards
• Ownership – You take charge of your work, uphold your commitments, and always do your best
• Commerciality – You focus on what matters most, ask questions when needed, and are cognizant about not wasting your time or that of others
• Humility – You welcome and are receptive to feedback and learn from past mistakes
• Adaptability – You can triage business needs and context switch quickly and efficiently
• Admirability – You elevate the room through your work ethic, domain knowledge, work product, and solution orientated attitude
 WE TAKE CARE OF OUR PEOPLE
We invest in our people, their careers, their health, and their well-being. When you work here, we provide:
• health care benefits
• Generous parental and family leave policies
• Mental and physical wellness programs
• Volunteer opportunities
• Non-profit matching gift program
• Support for employee-led affinity groups representing women, minorities and the LGBT+ community
• Tuition assistance

For more information, visit  www.Point72.com/working-here .

jobs.title: Corporate Concierge
jobs.description:
Corporate Concierge 
 About the Human Resources Department  
 The Human Resources Department at Bridgewater Associates is dedicated to strengthening the talent and systems that drive individual and organizational excellence—supporting our mission to develop a deep understanding of global economies and serve our clients with distinction. HR partners closely with business leaders across the full employee lifecycle, providing both strategic thought partnership and rigorous operational execution across recruiting, onboarding, compensation, benefits, performance, and workplace experience. 
 With an AI-first mindset, the team continuously builds capacity for higher-value work and improves the employee experience at scale. Our five core responsibilities span serving as subject matter experts on all people matters, running the processes that bring our talent strategy to life, ensuring every employee feels deeply cared for and celebrated, safeguarding the institution through disciplined compliance and governance, and building the infrastructure behind firm-wide people operations. 
 About Your Role 
 As the Corporate Concierge, you serve as a highly visible ambassador of the Workplace Experience team, creating an environment where employees and guests feel welcomed, supported, and enabled to do their best work. Acting with urgency, discretion, and a solutions-oriented mindset, you proactively address needs, drive resolution, and enhance the day-to-day experience of employees and guests. You thrive in a structured and service-oriented environment, value consistency and operational excellence, and work collaboratively across teams to ensure every interaction reflects the firm's high standards.
 You will drive the following responsibilities:     
 Serve as the primary point of contact for employees and guests, delivering welcoming, professional, and seamless onsite experience, including managing the internal and external calls that flow through the concierge desk.
 Build strong partnerships across the organization, using sound judgment and effective communication to address requests, solve problems, and support a variety of stakeholder needs.
 Proactively identify opportunities to improve the employee and guest experience through process enhancements, thoughtful service delivery, and continuous operational improvements.
 Manage workplace operations and concierge services with precision and consistency, ensuring efficient execution of daily processes and a high standard of service.
 Support Workplace Experience initiatives, projects, and events that advance team priorities and contribute to broader departmental goals.
 Contribute to a collaborative team environment by sharing knowledge, providing coverage, and adapting to evolving business needs.
 You will be on site 5 days per week and should be comfortable working at both our Westport, CT and New York City campuses.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 You are a service-minded professional who thrives in a structured, fast-paced environment and brings sound judgment, discretion, and strong communication to every interaction. To succeed in this role, you will need:
 A service-oriented mindset and genuine passion for creating positive employee and guest experiences.
 Sound judgment and the ability to navigate new, ambiguous, or evolving situations with professionalism and discretion.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor communication style, tone, and approach to different audiences and build strong relationships with employees, guests, and stakeholders.
 Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to effectively manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and follow-through.
 Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.
 Proficiency in workplace technology and collaboration tools, including Microsoft 365 applications (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint), Zoom Phone, and AI-enabled tools; comfort learning new technologies and systems.
 About Bridgewater 
 Bridgewater Associates is a global macro investment firm, founded in 1975, whose mission is to develop a fundamental, cause-and-effect understanding of how markets and economies work—and translate that understanding into insights, returns, and solutions that help the world’s leading institutional investors solve their most important investment challenges. 
 Over five decades, we have codified our fundamental understanding into a systematic investment process—integrating human judgment with machine intelligence with the goal of applying our thinking consistently, testing it against reality, and continuously improving decision-making over time. We believe this has created a unique platform for applying AI within our process, positioning us at the frontier of integrating technology with investment decision-making. 
 In financial markets—where reality is constantly evolving and outcomes are uncertain—sustained excellence requires continuous learning and improvement. Our culture—anchored in radical truth and transparency—helps us learn faster. 
 Find on our website .
 Our Culture 
 Bridgewater’s culture is anchored in the pursuit of excellence—tied directly to our mission. In financial markets, where the base case is failure and reality is constantly evolving, winning requires continuous learning and improvement. Truth is our most essential tool for improvement, and transparency helps us get closer to truth because it places many eyes on our decisions, problems, and mistakes. By understanding reality clearly, we can identify the gap between where we are and where we want to be—and use that knowledge to learn and get better. Our system that supports this way of being is an idea meritocracy, where we commit to finding and rewarding the best ideas regardless of hierarchy.
 Operating in these ways is hard. Finding truth and learning through it is inherently a high-friction cycle. It’s possible because we share a few core values: a commitment to honesty, high ownership, deeply meaningful work and relationships, and building Bridgewater as a big tent where vast differences are welcomed. These values create the common denominator that binds us together in good times and bad.
 Benefits 
 One of our core priorities at Bridgewater is to enable our employees to build a great life and career, and we believe our benefits are an important extension of that philosophy. As such, currently Bridgewater offers a competitive suite of benefits, including health insurance, retirement benefits, paid leave, and other fringe benefits. Find more information about Bridgewater’s benefits on our website .
 Bridgewater reserves the right to change its current benefits program at any time, in a manner that is consistent with applicable federal and state regulations.   
 Sponsorship 
 Please note that we do not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.  
 Compensation 
 The wage range for this role is $80,000-$95,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 80% - 90% of this wage range.   
 This job description is not a contract and confers no contractual rights, privileges, or benefits on any applicant or potential applicant. Bridgewater has the right to change any and all terms of this job description, including, but not limited to, job responsibilities, qualifications and benefits. Nothing in this job description constitutes an offer or guarantee of employment. 
 Bridgewater Associates, LP is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Data Sourcing & Strategy Associate
jobs.description:
About Bridgewater        
 Bridgewater Associates is a premier asset management firm, focused on delivering unique insight and partnership for the most sophisticated global institutional investors.         
 Our investment process is driven by a tireless pursuit to understand how the world’s markets and economies work — using cutting-edge technology to validate and execute on timeless and universal investment principles.         
 Founded in 1975, we are a community of independent thinkers who share a commitment to excellence. By fostering a culture of openness, transparency, and inclusion, we strive to unlock the most complex questions in investment strategy, management, and corporate culture.         
 Explore more information about Bridgewater on our website  here .    
 Our Culture        
 Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what's true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it's only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a  Philosophy Statement  which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on  Meritocracy.  Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else.    
 About Your Role     
 In this role, you will be an integral part of the Research, Data Strategy and Acquisition function at Bridgewater. Operating at the front edge of our Investment Data practice, you will be part of the execution and evolution of our Relationship Management, Supplier Knowledge Management, and Internal Stakeholder Management disciplines. You will engage with investors, associates, engineers, and external vendors and sources to improve our understanding of external offerings and vendors’ understanding of our needs, quality management, and business alignment.    
 You will be immersed in our workflows, investment questions, supplier challenges, market making and matching, internal marketing/advocacy, and vendor engagement strategy. You will regularly communicate your understanding and assessments to a diverse group of stakeholders, including investment professionals, vendors and service providers, Management, Compliance, Legal, and Finance. You will partner across the firm and with vendors (existing and prospective), collaborating with hundreds of individuals over the course of a year.    
 You will drive the following responsibilities:    
 Executing across the systems, sourcing, supply chains, and internal demand we use to acquire, provide and maintain the inbound fuel for the Investment requests that arrive unspecified or overly prescribed, helping the investor clarify what they need.   
 Dynamically understanding the world of offerings, known and unknown to Bridgewater, creating potential market matches, indications of interest, discerning and selecting structure from the external world.     
 Owning the Investment Asks that land unspecified or over-specified, where the investor or colleague cannot say what they need.   
 Understanding and effectively communicating the state of specific components of the sourcing portfolio, and our knowledge bases of passes, no bids, and deferred opportunities.     
 Building, maintaining, and rapidly sorting inbound possibilities, candidate sources and existing data sources and services in the sourcing portfolio.     
 Improving and executing on the ML/AI layer we are rapidly introducing into our external discovery and matching process, designed from first principles.   
 Creating and documenting initiatives to raise the quality, reliability, and efficiency of the practice’s systems.     
 Continuously evaluating and enhancing processes for sourcing, vetting, and delivering content processes at scale.     
 Advocating with existing and potential vendors to improve the quality of their pitches.     
 You will be a fit for the role if you:    
 Are curious, practical, analytical, capable, and willing to fail and learn from failing, in broad engagement with a diverse international set of people and processes both inside and outside of Bridgewater.     
 Are able to manage a high volume of work across diverse functions and competing priorities, while effectively communicating, executing and marking to market.     
 Think in terms of systems and naturally look for ways to solve problems through the evolution of those systems.     
 Hold a high degree of personal responsibility and ownership in everything you do.     
 Are willing to operate across all levels of work, starting from basic task execution and evolving into complex, multi-month and multi-modal efforts.     
 In this role, you will grow with us by:    
 Undergoing an on-the-job training program that includes structured engagement with the external world, live apprenticeship, and working with highly experienced colleagues.     
 Actively engaging and grappling with the growth and evolution of the practice.   
 Having your voice and perspective heard, and over time representing the firm in important vendor, counterparty, and provider management discussions.     
 Minimum Qualifications    
 4-year degree from an accredited undergraduate institution    
 3-7 years of relevant work experience at an investment bank, vendor/service provider or asset management firm    
 Experience in at least two of the following: Relationship Management, Supplier Knowledge Management (understanding what suppliers and sources can offer, beyond their past performance), or Internal Stakeholder Management  
 Experience with Capital Markets market or research data is a strong plus    
 Physical Requirements   
 The anticipated onsite requirement for this role is three days per week at our Westport, CT campus and one day per week at our NYC campus.    
 Compensation Band   
 The wage range for this role is $170,000-$225,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 70%-80% of this wage range.    
 Why Choose Bridgewater?

We develop people through an honest examination of their abilities and performance, enabling personal growth and professional development. We strive to provide you with opportunities that will challenge you and unlock your potential.

 The Business Process Improvement team focuses on improving processes across all Community Support. Our team is a global team of process improvement professionals, who help bring cross functional partners from across CS and Airbnb together to operationalize new processes, analyze current process for improvement opportunities, and scale solutions across a global network. We follow general business process engineering principles and practices, as well as leveraging Lean Six Sigma methodologies in our improvement projects. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 The Business Process Manager will be a senior individual contributor within the Service Optimization team, part of the Community Service Organization. This role advances the team's process engineering discipline by designing systems where problems do not occur, rather than only improving processes that already exist. The Business Process Manager delivers through deep individual expertise: applying systems thinking, engineering processes for AI-readiness and automation by default, and building AI prototypes to test and validate new process designs before full implementation. This is a role for a senior level practitioner who operates at the intersection of process engineering, systems design, and applied AI. 
 A Typical Day:  
 Develop business strategies within Service Optimization and Community Support across people, process, and technology.
 Lead the operationalization of strategies across Community Support and other cross functional teams such as Policy, Finance, and Product.
 Lead complex, large-scale, cross-functional process engineering initiatives from problem definition through measurable outcomes, applying the full suite of Lean Six Sigma tools and a structured process engineering framework across four disciplines: understanding the problem and its system context, designing reliable and measurable solutions, grounding those solutions in operational reality, and evolving them as conditions change.
 Apply and coach others to apply a systems thinking lens to every problem: map full upstream and downstream context before prescribing solutions, identifying where the real problem lives rather than where it surfaces.
 Design processes for AI-readiness and automation by default, engineering every future state around three standards: does it reduce agent and customer burden, is it measurable from day one, and can it be automated or self-correcting over time.
 Build AI prototypes to communicate and validate process designs, using AI tools, workflow automation platforms, and lightweight modeling approaches to test the viability of new process architectures before committing to full implementation.
 Use process simulation to model how a designed process will behave under real-world conditions, stress-testing assumptions about volume, variation, and failure modes before a design is deployed.

 Build and scale process engineering competency, systems thinking, and AI-ready design, contributing to capability building across the team.
 Partner with Product and Technology teams to translate process requirements into tooling specifications, ensuring AI and other product capabilities are engineered around how agents and customers actually work.

This team is responsible for developing and scaling new growth levers for Airbnb. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role.

jobs.title: Regional Workplace Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join:  
 The Regional Workplace Operations Manager sits at the intersection of workplace experience, events, and gathering & culture. This role is responsible for bringing our brand to life by creating an intentional, welcoming, and high-functioning office experience that enables employees, leaders, and guests to feel connected, productive, and inspired. Just like our hosts can offer differentiated experiences to our guests, our Regional Workplace Operations Manager exemplifies those aspirational expectations.  
 This role serves as the connective tissue across office operations, hospitality, employee engagement, and local community experience. They partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders including Talent, IT, Security, Communications, Executive Support, and local leaders to ensure each office reflects Airbnb’s culture and values in a meaningful and scalable way. They integrate platform hosts in the day to day office experience spotlighting service and experience hosts as appropriate. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 As the Regional Workplace Operations Manager, you are the primary steward of the employee and guest experience within your office. You create a hospitality-forward environment where people feel welcomed, supported, and connected to Airbnb and each other. 
 You will oversee the daily office experience while also leading local gathering and engagement efforts that strengthen culture and community. You will direct and coordinate embedded vendors and operational partners to ensure seamless execution across hospitality, food, facilities, and events. You will provide oversight and mentorship to Office Managers within your region, ensuring consistency of standards and experience across proximate offices. 
 Success in this role requires strong operational ownership, exceptional interpersonal instincts, creativity, and the ability to navigate ambiguity while balancing both strategic thinking and hands-on execution. 
 You must have your finger on the pulse and anticipate the needs of each guest. 
 A Typical Day:  
 Lead Through Hospitality 
 Maintain a visible, approachable, and highly responsive presence within the office community. 
 Create a warm, thoughtful, and highly responsive environment where employees and visitors feel genuinely welcomed and cared for. 
 Lead with calmness, flexibility, and attention to detail while balancing multiple priorities and adapting to changing business needs. 
 Support and guide vendors and partners to operate as one cohesive hospitality team in service of the office community. 
 Drive Operational Excellence 
 Establish and maintain office operating standards that ensure consistency of hospitality, communication, service delivery, and workplace experience. 
 Monitor office utilization, employee feedback, operational performance, and service quality to identify opportunities for improvement. 
 Contribute local insights and best practices that help shape the evolution of workplace standards across the broader portfolio. 
 Develop repeatable processes and playbooks that enable scalable, high-quality office experiences. 
 Own the Office Experience 
 Oversee the holistic daily office experience, ensuring the space operates smoothly and delivers a welcoming, hospitality-forward environment for employees and guests. 
 You have a strong sense of ownership. Treat the office as your listing.  
 Serve as the day-to-day steward of the office environment, ensuring the space is operationally seamless, hospitality-forward, and consistently ready to support great work, connection, and high-visibility moments. 
 Provide operational oversight and direction to on-site vendors and service partners. 
 Direct and orchestrate on-site vendors and operational vendors including food, facilities, events, and hospitality to ensure consistent service delivery and experience quality. Own escalation management and drive resolution 
 Partner closely with Security, IT and other operational teams to ensure seamless day-to-day operations. 
 Act as the “Voice of the Office,” helping employees navigate the workplace experience and ensuring the office feels connected, informed, and supported. 
 Monitor employee sentiment and proactively identify opportunities to improve the office experience, communication, and engagement. 
 Enable Gathering & Engagement Experiences 
 Ensure the office is consistently prepared to support high-visibility visits, events, and business moments. 
 Partner with Regional Gathering Programs to support successful delivery of offsites, leadership visits and strategic gatherings. 
 Provide local stakeholder coordination, hospitality leadership, vendor management, and onsite execution support as needed. 
 Support onsite execution for local events, offsites, and engagement activities, ensuring thoughtful hospitality, operational excellence, and strong attendee experience. 
 Adapt office experiences to local needs while maintaining consistency with Airbnb culture and values. 
 Build Strong Partnerships 
 Develop strong relationships with local leaders, executive admins, Airfinity groups, cross-functional partners and other key stakeholders. 
 Act as a trusted partner and connector across teams, helping identify opportunities to strengthen office culture, engagement, and employee experience. 
 Partner with leaders to support meaningful moments of connection within the office and across teams. 
 Your Expertise: 
 6–9+ years of experience in workplace experience, hospitality, events, employee engagement, operations, or related fields 
 Experience owning and executing programs, events, or operational experiences end-to-end 
 Strong hospitality mindset with a passion for creating thoughtful and high-quality experiences 
 Experience managing vendors, operational partners, or service delivery teams 
 Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills across diverse teams and leadership levels 
 Ability to operate autonomously, navigate ambiguity, and manage multiple priorities simultaneously 
 Strong organizational and operational execution skills with attention to detail 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills 
 Experience supporting employee engagement, cultural programming, gatherings, or community-building initiatives is preferred 
 Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution 
 Passion for Airbnb’s mission, culture, and values

 This role is expected to be based in-office full-time in our New York office, with flexibility for occasional evenings or weekends in support of events and gatherings.
